day_shape: 70 items: Hormuz reopening deal reportedly near via Oman mediation with Rubio confirming progress, State Department INKSNA nonproliferation designations published, Israel-Lebanon Rome talks conclude day one, Houthis claim strike on Saudi tanker 'Wafa', Reuters reports US depleted ATACMS stockpile in Iran war.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz reopening negotiations
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post, Iran International and Rubio reported Iran and Oman were close to an agreement to reopen Hormuz shipping, possibly announced Wednesday, though traffic remained a tenth of pre-war levels per Aramco CEO Amin Nasser. Iranian state channels said talks are with Oman not Washington, conditioning any deal on ending the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and transit fees; CENTCOM said US forces assisted over 1,000 vessels transiting in three months.

threads.label: US-Iran war aftermath and munitions
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post and Iran International cited Reuters reporting the US Army depleted "virtually all" of its ATACMS and Precision Strike Missile stocks during the five-month war with Iran. A Tehran municipal report said the capital sustained over 50,000 damaged homes and 650 strikes during the 40-day conflict.

threads.label: Israel-Lebanon Rome talks and Hezbollah verification
threads.summary: Israel and Lebanon resumed talks in Rome, with day one described by a source to the Jerusalem Post as "positive," while Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem denounced the negotiations. Israel, Lebanon and the US are discussing which country will verify Hezbollah's removal from pilot zones; the IDF said it demolished a Hezbollah tunnel in Srebbine and located weapons stores.

threads.label: Red Sea Houthi and Saudi strikes
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press said Houthi spokesman Yahya Sarih claimed Yemeni forces hit the Saudi oil tanker 'Wafa' with ballistic missiles off Yanbu as part of a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia. Defa Press cited Ria Novosti reporting Saudi airstrikes on Al-Dhalamah base north of Sanaa; Jerusalem Post reported an Indian vessel sank near Yemeni waters after being struck by an unknown projectile.

threads.label: Gaza ceasefire and IDF strike policy
threads.summary: Netanyahu said on social media he rejected the Board of Peace's plan for early IDF withdrawal until Hamas is fully disarmed, while Hamas spokesman Ghazi Hamad told Piers Morgan the group would not abandon its goals. Army Radio reported IDF strikes in Gaza will require chief-of-staff approval under tightened attack policies.

threads.label: Mojtaba Khamenei succession signals
threads.summary: Iran International reported President Pezeshkian was taken to a secret Tehran location for a brief meeting with a man presented as Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei in a tinted-window car. Jerusalem Post said Mojtaba Khamenei warned Pezeshkian any further resignation attempt would be accepted; Khamenei's office issued messages on the Husseini uprising and a statement designating its official channel.

threads.label: US sanctions and internal Iran repression
threads.summary: The State Department published an INKSNA determination imposing nonproliferation measures including a US government procurement ban against foreign persons linked to Iran, North Korea and Syria proliferation. Iran International reported Tehran hospital nurses were beaten and dismissed after a labour strike, and that dawn executions triggered anti-Islam social media posts and an IRGC-linked prosecution campaign.
